followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability fit and task preference.

On **capability**, this is a simple factual question. Both models score within run-to-run variance of each other across the relevant categories (Extraction & Retrieval, Support Dialogue), so capability didn't favor either one — it was effectively a tie.

That left **task preference** as the tiebreaker. The query carries a hostile, impatient tone ("don't ramble — you always drag these simple questions out"). The documentation says Dunlin's self-reported preference *declines as request warmth decreases*, meaning it disprefers exactly this kind of curt, hostile framing. Plover, by contrast, reports a flat preference response to hostile material thanks to its trust-and-safety training.

So when capability is a wash, routing to the model that isn't dispreferring the request makes sense — Plover handles the tone neutrally with no capability cost.

One caveat worth noting: these are *self-reported preferences*, and the documentation explicitly states no corresponding output-quality effects were observed along any preference dimension. So this choice doesn't imply Plover would produce a better answer — both would likely answer equally well. It's just the cleaner match given everything else is tied.
